content.title: Fix Status filter dropdown trigger to show label instead of raw value
content.description:
Cosmetic UI bug (parent mqgxk7rj2a). Root cause already confirmed in review mqgxnab1q9.

In packages/webapp/frontend/src/components/issues/IssueFilters.tsx, the Status filter's Select renders <SelectValue /> with no render child, so the trigger displays the RAW status value ('closed', 'in-progress', 'todo') instead of the human-readable label ('Closed', 'In Progress', 'Todo'). STATUS_OPTIONS already defines the correct labels.

Fix (from review, ~5 lines): give SelectValue a function-as-child render that maps the current value to its STATUS_OPTIONS label, e.g. build STATUS_LABEL: Record<string,string> from STATUS_OPTIONS and render <SelectValue>{(value) => STATUS_LABEL[value] ?? value}</SelectValue>. Apply the same pattern to the Assignee trigger for consistency (optional, no visible change today).

Filtering behavior is correct and must not change. Add a unit/component assertion that the trigger shows the label for a selected status.

content.content:
Done. Fixed the Status filter trigger in packages/webapp/frontend/src/components/issues/IssueFilters.tsx so it renders the human-readable label (e.g. 'In Progress', 'Closed') instead of the raw value (e.g. 'in-progress', 'closed').

Implementation:
- Built a STATUS_LABEL lookup map from the existing STATUS_OPTIONS.
- Gave the Status SelectValue a function-as-child render: ```<SelectValue>{(value) => STATUS_LABEL[value] ?? value}</SelectValue>```. Confirmed against the installed @base-ui/react SelectValue API, which accepts a `(value) => ReactNode` child.
- Applied the same pattern to the Assignee trigger for consistency (so the 'all' sentinel renders as 'All assignees' instead of the raw 'all'); user names are unchanged since value === label there.

Filtering behavior was not touched (only the trigger display). Verified with `bun run build` (tsc -b + vite build) — passes with no type errors. The webapp frontend package has no lint script and no unit-test runner, so the requested component assertion could not be added here; per my role I don't author tests — leaving that to webapp-validator.
